rows.claim: lane_supervisor was built from the operator complaint 'i have to babysit the lane otherwise it errors out'; the answer is a cheap automated probe for every configured lane, not more human attention.
rows.quote: Every configured lane gets a cheap probe. State machine per lane:
rows.steal: When a human reports having to keep nudging a component, convert the complaint into a scheduled minimal probe of that component instead of adding attention.
rows.falsifier: A lane erroring out with no matching row appended in state/fuel/lane_health.jsonl means probes did not replace watching.

rows.claim: Lane health is a per-lane state machine with a 3-consecutive-fail DOWN threshold and a RECOVERED state, so single transient failures never page anyone; state is rebuilt from the log tail, not held in memory.
rows.quote: UP -> (fail) FLAKING -> (3 consecutive fails) DOWN -> (pass again) RECOVERED
rows.steal: Any health check that alarms on first failure is wrong; require a streak counter rebuilt from a log tail so flapping is absorbed and recovery is a first-class event.
rows.falsifier: A single transient fail producing state DOWN, or a pass after DOWN that never yields RECOVERED, falsifies the machine.

rows.claim: Lanes are grouped into capability classes and each class names its fallback chain; a class is served if ANY member is not DOWN, so single-lane death is invisible to consumers and only whole-class death escalates.
rows.quote: Failover: each lane class names its fallback chain; a DOWN lane's class is served
rows.steal: Group interchangeable providers into classes and declare the class UP if one member lives; only the all-members-DOWN case rises to a human or a caller.
rows.falsifier: A class listed in classes_without_failover while one member is not DOWN (or a caller blocked by a DOWN lane whose class sibling is UP) falsifies the ladder.

rows.law: escalation is a decision, not a task
rows.claim: Escalation to the operator's phone is the last rung only: it fires exclusively when a lane class is DOWN with no failover left, and escalation failure must never crash the probe.
rows.steal: Reserve the operator channel for undecidable cases only; anything decidable by failover, retry, or state transitions never reaches the phone.
rows.falsifier: Any phone escalation fired while a failover sibling in the same class was UP proves escalation leaked below the last rung.

rows.law: schtask full-path law (bare python on PATH is the Hermes trap)
rows.claim: Scheduled tasks must pin the absolute repo interpreter: improve_daily.ps1 binds the full .venv python path and execs main.py through it; the a741defc5 catch was that three new tasks registered with bare python hit Task Scheduler's clean PATH (0x80070002) while hand-fires worked, and on this box bare python is the Hermes venv with no Mag deps.
rows.steal: Every schtask /TR on this estate gets the absolute .venv interpreter path (or a ps1 wrapper that pins it) and an existence check before run; never bare python, because PATH under the scheduler is clean and bare python on the interactive PATH is Hermes.
rows.falsifier: A registered task whose Task To Run contains bare python, or any scheduled run dying with 0x80070002 or 'No module named langgraph' under the scheduler, falsifies the law.
